triviaItems.fact: The Maasai Mara safari reserve is in Kenya.

cards.name: Kiribati
cards.story: Britain imposed colonial rule over the Gilbert Islands in 1892 and phosphate-rich Banaba (Ocean Island), where British strip-mining devastated the island—leading colonial authorities to forcibly relocate the entire Banaban population (~1,000 people) to Rabi Island in Fiji after World War II's brutal Japanese occupation and Battle of Tarawa (~6,000 dead). After the Ellice Islands split away as Tuvalu, Kiribati gained independence in 1979.

environment.summary: Kiribati consists of thirty-three low-lying coral atolls and one raised reef island scattered across 3.5 million square kilometers of equatorial Pacific Ocean.

triviaItems.fact: Te Mwaie, a frigatebird-inspired dance performed in traditional maneaba meeting houses, is a signature art of Kiribati.

cards.name: Kosovo
cards.story: After Serbia stripped Kosovo's autonomy within Yugoslavia in 1989, the 1998–99 Kosovo War saw Serbian and Yugoslav forces kill over 10,000 Kosovar Albanians and conduct mass ethnic cleansing that forcibly expelled roughly 850,000–900,000 Albanians across borders (over half the population) before NATO airstrikes forced a withdrawal—followed by retaliatory expulsions of over 100,000 Kosovo Serbs and Roma. Administered by the UN, Kosovo declared independence in 2008.
cards.contestedNote: Kosovo declared independence in 2008 after the 1998–99 war and ethnic cleansing; over 100 countries recognize its statehood, while Serbia and several other nations do not.

environment.summary: Kosovo comprises two fertile highland plains framed by the Accursed Mountains (Prokletije) and Šar Mountains, with glacial lakes, beech forests, and karst river gorges.

triviaItems.fact: DokuFest, an acclaimed international documentary film festival in historic Prizren, is hosted in Kosovo.

cards.name: Kuwait
cards.story: Founded as a Gulf trading town in the 1700s, Kuwait accepted British colonial protection in 1899, and a 1922 British-imposed border treaty fixed its desert lines with Iraq and Saudi Arabia before independence in 1961. In August 1990, Iraq invaded and occupied Kuwait for seven months—killing over 1,000 Kuwaitis, displacing roughly 400,000 residents, and torching hundreds of oil wells—before a U.S.-led coalition expelled Iraqi forces in the 1991 Gulf War (which also led to the expulsion of ~300,000–400,000 Palestinian residents from Kuwait).

environment.biomeLabel: Arid Persian Gulf Desert & Tidal Flats
environment.summary: Kuwait consists of flat sandy and gravel desert plains bordering the shallow waters, tidal mudflats, and coral islets of Kuwait Bay and the northwestern Persian Gulf.

triviaItems.fact: Traditional wooden dhow shipbuilding and Diwaniya community reception halls are cultural hallmarks of Kuwait.

cards.name: Kyrgyzstan
cards.story: Conquered by the Russian Empire in the 1800s, Kyrgyz communities rose against imperial conscription and settler land seizures in the 1916 Central Asian Revolt (Urkun), which Russian troops crushed with massacres and forced flight across the Tian Shan mountains into China that killed an estimated 100,000 to 270,000 Kyrgyz and Kazakhs. Soviet boundary planners drew Kyrgyzstan's republic borders in the 1920s–30s; independent since 1991, ethnic clashes in southern Osh in 2010 killed hundreds and displaced ~400,000.

environment.biomeLabel: High Alpine Tian Shan & Mountain Steppe
environment.summary: More than 90% of Kyrgyzstan is mountainous, dominated by glaciated Tian Shan ridges, walnut forests, alpine summer pastures, and high-altitude Lake Issyk-Kul.

triviaItems.fact: The World Nomad Games and the monumental oral Epic of Manas originated in Kyrgyzstan.

cards.name: Laos
cards.story: Tracing its roots to the Kingdom of Lan Xang, Laos's Mekong borders were fixed in 1893 when France forced Siam to cede eastern territories into French Indochina before independence in 1953. During the Vietnam War's 'Secret War' (1964–73), the United States dropped over 2 million tons of bombs on Laos—making it the most heavily bombed country per capita in history—killing an estimated 50,000 to 200,000 Laotians, displacing roughly 700,000 (a quarter of the population), and forcing over 300,000 refugees (including many Hmong) abroad.

environment.summary: Steep karst limestone ridges, dense Annamite forests, and the cool Bolaven Plateau drain into the winding Mekong River floodplain.

triviaItems.fact: Boun Pi Mai New Year celebrations in Luang Prabang and the golden That Luang Festival take place in Laos.

cards.name: Latvia
cards.story: Latvia won independence from imperial Russia in 1918–20 before the Soviet Union forcibly annexed it in 1940, followed by Nazi German occupation (1941–44) and renewed Soviet rule. During WWII, Nazi forces and local collaborators murdered roughly 70,000 Latvian Jews (~90% of the Jewish population), while Soviet deportations in 1941 and 1949 sent over 57,000 Latvians to Siberian gulags and ~150,000+ fled into exile before independence was restored in 1991.

environment.summary: More than half of Latvia is forested with pine and birch, crisscrossed by winding rivers, raised peat bogs, glacial lakes, and long sandy Baltic beaches.

triviaItems.fact: The midsummer Jāņi festival of oak-leaf crowns, bonfires, and folk songs is celebrated across Latvia.

cards.name: Lebanon
cards.story: After the Ottoman Empire collapsed—following the 1915–18 Great Famine of Mount Lebanon that killed an estimated 150,000 to 200,000 people—France carved Greater Lebanon out of Syria in 1920 before independence in 1943. Confessional divisions, regional wars, Israeli invasions/occupations (1978–2000 and 2024), and the 1975–90 Lebanese Civil War killed roughly 120,000 to 150,000 people and displaced nearly 1 million; Lebanon also shelters over 1 million Palestinian and Syrian refugees.

environment.summary: A narrow coastal strip climbs sharply up the snow-dusted Mount Lebanon range—home to ancient cedar groves—before dropping into the fertile Bekaa Valley.

triviaItems.fact: The Baalbeck International Festival stages music inside monumental Roman temple ruins in Lebanon.

cards.name: Lesotho
cards.story: Founded by King Moshoeshoe I in the 1820s as a mountain sanctuary during the devastating Mfecane regional upheavals, the Basotho kingdom lost much of its fertile western lowlands in wars with Boer settlers before seeking British protection in 1868 to avoid complete annexation. Entirely surrounded by South Africa, Lesotho gained independence in 1966 along those shrunken borders.

environment.summary: Lesotho is the only country lying entirely above 1,000 meters, marked by basalt Drakensberg and Maloti plateaus, alpine grasslands, and deep river gorges.

triviaItems.fact: The conical woven mokorotlo hat (featured on the national flag) and Basotho wool blankets are icons of Lesotho.

cards.name: Liberia
cards.story: Established in the 1820s by the American Colonization Society for freed African Americans—whose settler elite marginalized and fought Indigenous coastal and interior peoples—Liberia declared independence in 1847 while British and French colonial empires later stripped away parts of its frontier. Two devastating civil wars between 1989 and 2003 killed an estimated 250,000 people and displaced over 1 million—nearly a third of the country.

environment.summary: Liberia rises from humid Atlantic mangrove coasts into rolling hills cloaked in West Africa's largest remaining tracts of Upper Guinean rainforest.

triviaItems.fact: Founded by formerly enslaved African Americans alongside Indigenous peoples, Liberia celebrates Flag Day and rich mask-carving traditions.

cards.name: Libya
cards.story: Italy invaded Ottoman Libya in 1911 and waged a ruthless two-decade war to crush Senussi resistance: between 1929 and 1934, Fascist Italy forcibly marched roughly 100,000 Cyrenaican Bedouin civilians into desert concentration camps where an estimated 50,000 to 70,000 died from execution, starvation, and disease before Italy united three provinces into Libya in 1934. Independent in 1951 after Italy's WWII defeat, post-2011 civil conflicts have killed tens of thousands and displaced hundreds of thousands.

environment.summary: More than 90% of Libya consists of arid Saharan sand seas, rocky plateaus, and oasis depressions, bordered in the north by a narrow Mediterranean coastal belt.

triviaItems.fact: The historic oasis town of Ghadames and the Roman theater of Leptis Magna lie in Libya.

cards.name: Liechtenstein
cards.turningPoint: 1806 End of the Holy Roman Empire
cards.story: Formed when the Liechtenstein family united two small Alpine estates in 1719, this microstate gained full sovereignty when Napoleon dissolved the Holy Roman Empire in 1806. Neutrality and close economic ties with Switzerland have kept its borders unchanged for over two centuries.

environment.summary: Liechtenstein is a compact Alpine principality rising from fertile Upper Rhine floodplains to steep forested slopes and rugged Rätikon limestone peaks.

triviaItems.fact: Liechtenstein is entirely within the Alps and has no army.

cards.name: Lithuania
cards.story: Once part of a vast medieval Grand Duchy, Lithuania won independence in 1918 before Poland seized Vilnius (1920) and the USSR forcibly annexed the country in 1940 (returning Vilnius). During Nazi occupation (1941–44), Germans and local collaborators murdered roughly 195,000 to 200,000 Lithuanian Jews (~90–95% of its Jewish community), while Soviet deportations and post-war anti-Soviet partisan warfare (1944–53) killed over 20,000 and deported ~130,000 to Siberia before Lithuania led the break from the USSR in 1990.

environment.summary: Lithuania features rolling glacial hills, pine-and-oak woodlands, thousands of lakes, the Nemunas River basin, and the sweeping coastal dunes of the Curonian Spit.

triviaItems.fact: Užgavėnės, a masked winter-farewell festival featuring pancakes and wooden masks, is celebrated in Lithuania.

cards.name: Luxembourg
cards.story: Carved out by the 1839 Treaty of London—which transferred its larger French-speaking western half to Belgium—Luxembourg had its neutrality guaranteed in 1867. Despite neutrality, Germany invaded and occupied Luxembourg in both World Wars, forcibly conscripting over 10,000 Luxembourgers into the Wehrmacht and murdering ~1,300 to 2,000 Jews from its small Jewish population during the Holocaust.

environment.summary: Luxembourg combines the rocky forested valleys of the northern Oesling (Ardennes) with fertile southern Gutland farmland and Moselle wine-growing riverbanks.

triviaItems.fact: The Schueberfouer, a grand fair founded in 1340, is held each late summer in Luxembourg.

cards.name: Madagascar
cards.story: Unified largely under the Merina Kingdom, Madagascar was invaded and annexed by France in 1895–96 after a war that killed thousands and abolished the monarchy. When Malagasy nationalists rose up against French colonial rule in 1947–48, French forces crushed the rebellion through mass executions, village burnings, and induced famine that killed an estimated 30,000 to 100,000 people before independence arrived in 1960.

environment.summary: Long isolated in the Indian Ocean, Madagascar spans lush eastern rainforests, central highlands, western baobab dry forests, and southern spiny desert filled with endemic wildlife.

triviaItems.fact: The Avenue of the Baobabs is a famous landmark in Madagascar.
Madagascar is the largest island nation in Africa.
Lemurs are found in the wild only on Madagascar.

cards.name: Malawi
cards.story: Devastated in the 19th century by the East African slave trade, the Lake Malawi basin was claimed by Britain as Nyasaland in 1891 via imperial treaties with Portugal, imposing harsh colonial hut taxes and plantation labor that sparked John Chilembwe's 1915 uprising. After resisting a white-minority colonial federation—during which British forces killed dozens in the 1959 State of Emergency—Malawi won independence in 1964.

environment.biomeLabel: East African Rift Lake & Highland Plateau
environment.summary: Malawi is dominated by deep, biodiverse Lake Malawi along the Great Rift Valley, flanked by forested Nyika plateaus and granite Mount Mulanje.

triviaItems.fact: The UNESCO-listed Gule Wamkulu masked dance of the Chewa people and the Lake of Stars arts festival are cultural highlights of Malawi.

cards.name: Malaysia
cards.story: Britain consolidated colonial control over Malaya and northern Borneo through treaties and military interventions, building tin and rubber economies on mass Chinese and Indian labor migration; Japan's 1941–45 occupation killed tens of thousands, followed by the 1948–60 Malayan Emergency counterinsurgency in which Britain forcibly relocated ~500,000 mostly ethnic Chinese civilians into fenced 'New Villages' and killed ~11,000. Malaya (1957) joined Sabah, Sarawak, and Singapore in 1963 before Singapore's 1965 separation.

environment.summary: Malaysia splits between Peninsular Malaysia's ancient Taman Negara rainforest and limestone hills, and Malaysian Borneo's towering Mount Kinabalu and river jungles.

triviaItems.fact: The vibrant Thaipusam pilgrimage up the rainbow steps of Batu Caves and Hari Raya open houses take place in Malaysia.

cards.name: Maldives
cards.story: Comprising roughly 1,200 Indian Ocean coral islands, the Maldives resisted a brutal 15-year Portuguese colonial occupation (1558–73) before entering a British protectorate treaty in 1887 that gave Britain control of its foreign policy and strategic southern airbases. The archipelago regained full independence from Britain in 1965.

environment.summary: The Maldives comprises nearly 1,200 low-lying coral islands grouped into 26 natural ring-shaped atolls surrounded by turquoise lagoons and Indian Ocean reefs.

triviaItems.fact: Bodu Beru coconut-wood drumming and coral-stone mosques characterize the island culture of the Maldives.

cards.name: Mali
cards.story: Home to the medieval empires of Ghana, Mali, and Songhai, the region was invaded and conquered by France in the late 1800s as French Sudan, crushing local resistance and imposing forced labor while splitting Tuareg and other nomadic peoples across colonial borders. Independent since 1960, rebellions and Sahel conflicts since 2012 have killed over 15,000 people and displaced hundreds of thousands.

environment.biomeLabel: Sahara Desert, Sahel & Niger Inland Delta
environment.summary: Mali transitions from arid northern Saharan dunes through dry Sahel plains to the seasonally flooded wetlands of the Inner Niger Delta and southern savannas.

triviaItems.fact: The 21-string kora harp and griot (jali) oral storytelling are deeply rooted musical traditions of Mali.
The djembe goblet drum and Mandinka balafon traditions flourished across the Upper Niger region of Mali.
The legendary city of Timbuktu is in Mali.

cards.name: Malta
cards.story: Positioned at a strategic Mediterranean choke point, Malta was ruled successively by Phoenicians, the Knights of St. John, Napoleon's France, and the British Empire from 1800 onward. During World War II, relentless Axis aerial bombardments made Malta one of the most heavily bombed places on Earth, killing over 1,500 civilians and destroying thousands of buildings before Malta gained independence from Britain in 1964.

environment.summary: Malta consists of sun-drenched honey-colored limestone islands sculpted into sea cliffs, natural harbors, rocky scrubland, and clear central Mediterranean waters.

cards.name: Marshall Islands
cards.story: Passed from German and Japanese colonial rule into a U.S.-run UN Trust Territory after fierce World War II battles at Kwajalein and Enewetak (~10,000+ combatant deaths), the Marshall Islands endured 67 U.S. nuclear weapons tests between 1946 and 1958—including the 1954 Castle Bravo thermonuclear blast. The tests contaminated atolls with radioactive fallout, caused generational radiation illnesses, and forcibly displaced islanders from Bikini, Enewetak, Rongelap, and Utrik before independence in 1986.

environment.summary: The Marshall Islands comprises twenty-nine narrow coral atolls and five isolated islands arranged in two parallel chains across the central Pacific.

triviaItems.fact: Traditional woven stick charts mapping ocean-swell refraction between coral atolls were pioneered by navigators from the Marshall Islands.

cards.name: Mauritania
cards.story: France militarily conquered Saharan emirates in the early 1900s and drew geometric desert borders combining Arab-Berber and Black West African communities into Mauritania before independence in 1960. Border tensions and ethnic violence with Senegal in 1989–91 led Mauritania's regime to kill hundreds and forcibly expel roughly 60,000 to 75,000 Black Mauritanians across the Senegal River.

environment.biomeLabel: Sahara Desert & Rich Atlantic Upwelling Coast
environment.summary: Sweeping Saharan dunes and sandstone plateaus meet cold nutrient-rich Atlantic currents at Banc d'Arguin, creating vital coastal wetlands for migratory birds.

triviaItems.fact: The ancient desert manuscript libraries of Chinguetti and Moorish tidinit lute music are cultural treasures of Mauritania.

cards.name: Mauritius
cards.story: Uninhabited before European colonization, Dutch, French, and British empires built Mauritius's sugar economy on hundreds of thousands of enslaved Africans and, after abolition, over 450,000 Indian indentured laborers. Before granting independence in 1968, Britain unlawfully detached the Chagos Islands and forcibly expelled the entire Indigenous Chagossian population—roughly 1,500 to 2,000 people—to build a U.S.–UK military base on Diego Garcia.
cards.contestedNote: Britain forcibly expelled roughly 1,500–2,000 Chagossians between 1968 and 1973 after detaching the Chagos Archipelago from Mauritius; following a 2019 ICJ advisory opinion, the UK and Mauritius signed a May 2025 sovereignty transfer treaty, though as of late 2026 UK ratification remains stalled and Chagossian right-of-return disputes persist.

environment.summary: Mauritius is ringed by one of the world's largest unbroken coral reefs and rises inland to volcanic peaks, sugarcane plains, waterfalls, and remnant ebony forests.

triviaItems.fact: UNESCO-listed Sega music and dance—born among enslaved communities on sugar plantations—is the national cultural art of Mauritius.

cards.name: Mexico
cards.story: Spain's 1519–21 conquest of the Aztec Empire and subsequent colonial rule triggered a catastrophic collapse of Mexico's Indigenous population—dropping from roughly 15–25 million to ~1–2 million within a century from epidemics, warfare, and forced labor. After winning independence in 1821, Mexico lost roughly half its national territory to the United States through Texas's secession and the 1846–48 U.S.–Mexico War, and later suffered 1 to 2 million deaths during the 1910–20 Mexican Revolution.

environment.summary: Mexico spans extraordinary geographic diversity, uniting Sonoran and Chihuahuan deserts, pine-oak Sierra Madre ranges, central volcanic plateaus, Pacific reefs, and Yucatán jungle cenotes.

triviaItems.fact: The Day of the Dead is a major celebration in Mexico.
Tacos and tamales are traditional foods of Mexico.
Chichén Itzá, the Maya pyramid, is in Mexico.
The Aztec Empire was centered in modern-day Mexico.
Mexico is home to Cozumel, the busiest cruise port of call in the Caribbean.

cards.name: Micronesia
cards.story: Colonized successively by Spain (whose 1887–90 wars crushed Pohnpeian resistance), Germany (which killed and exiled hundreds in the 1910–11 Sokehs Rebellion), and Japan—whose World War II militarization and U.S. bombardments at Chuuk Lagoon killed thousands of soldiers and Micronesians—the islands passed to a U.S.-run UN Trust Territory before four island states united as independent Micronesia in 1986.

environment.summary: The Federated States of Micronesia spans over 600 western Pacific islands, combining lush volcanic peaks on Pohnpei, Kosrae, Chuuk, and Yap with outer coral atolls.

triviaItems.fact: The ancient basalt-log canal city of Nan Madol on Pohnpei and Yap's giant carved Rai stone discs are iconic heritage sites of Micronesia.

cards.name: Moldova
cards.story: Carved out in 1940 when the Soviet Union seized Bessarabia from Romania—followed by Stalinist deportations of over 60,000 Moldovans to Siberia and the WWII Romanian-Nazi Holocaust murdering an estimated 200,000 to 300,000 Jews across Bessarabia, Bukovina, and Transnistria—Moldova became independent in 1991. A 1992 war over the Russian-backed breakaway region of Transnistria killed ~1,000 people and displaced over 100,000.
cards.contestedNote: The eastern strip of Transnistria has operated as a Russian-backed breakaway territory since the 1992 conflict (~1,000 killed, ~100,000+ displaced), though it remains internationally recognized as part of Moldova.

environment.summary: Moldova consists of fertile black-earth hills, orchards, and vineyards nestled between the winding Dniester and Prut rivers.

cards.name: Monaco
cards.story: Ruled by the Grimaldi dynasty since 1297, Monaco surrendered the neighboring Riviera towns of Menton and Roquebrune to France in the 1861 treaty in exchange for formal French recognition of its compact coastal borders. During World War II, Axis occupation resulted in the arrest and deportation of roughly 90 Jews from Monaco to Nazi death camps.

environment.summary: Monaco sits on a steep limestone headland where the Maritime Alps plunge directly into the warm Ligurian Sea along the French Riviera.

triviaItems.fact: One of motorsport's most famous street-circuit Grand Prix races winds past Monte Carlo in Monaco.

cards.name: Mongolia
cards.story: Once the core of the 13th-century Mongol Empire, Outer Mongolia broke away from China's Qing Dynasty in 1911 and established independence in 1921 with Soviet military backing, leaving Inner Mongolia inside China. Under Soviet-aligned rule, the 1937–39 Great Repression executed an estimated 22,000 to 35,000 people—including roughly 18,000 Buddhist monks—and destroyed over 700 monasteries before Mongolia transitioned to democracy in 1990.

environment.biomeLabel: Highland Steppe, Gobi Desert & Altai Peaks
environment.summary: Mongolia spans wind-swept nomadic grasslands and arid Gobi gravel deserts framed by the snowy Altai Mountains in the west and Siberian taiga in the north.

triviaItems.fact: Genghis Khan founded an empire based in Mongolia.

cards.name: Montenegro
cards.story: An independent mountain principality that fought Ottoman forces for centuries before being absorbed into Yugoslavia in 1918, Montenegro suffered tens of thousands of deaths during World War II's Axis occupation and partisan warfare. Remaining federated with Serbia during Yugoslavia's 1990s breakup—when Montenegrin units took part in shelling Dubrovnik and sheltering tens of thousands of Bosnian and Kosovar refugees—Montenegro voted narrowly in a 2006 referendum to restore independence.

environment.summary: Steep dark-forested limestone peaks of Durmitor and Lovćen plunge dramatically into the Bay of Kotor and deep turquoise Tara River canyon.

triviaItems.fact: The Kotor Winter Carnival takes place inside a UNESCO-listed fjord-like bay in Montenegro.

cards.name: Morocco
cards.story: France and Spain forced Morocco into colonial protectorates in 1912 and waged bloody pacification wars—including Spain's use of chemical mustard-gas bombs during the 1920s Rif War—that killed tens of thousands before Morocco regained independence in 1956. In 1975, Morocco militarily occupied most of neighboring Western Sahara, sparking a 16-year war and displacing roughly 170,000 Sahrawi refugees.
cards.contestedNote: Morocco occupies and administers most of Western Sahara as its Southern Provinces, while the UN classifies Western Sahara as a non-self-governing territory whose final status remains unresolved.

environment.summary: Morocco spans Mediterranean and Atlantic coastlines, snow-capped High Atlas ranges, cedar-clad Rif hills, and golden Saharan dunes.

triviaItems.fact: The Fes Festival of World Sacred Music and UNESCO-listed Gnawa music traditions take place in Morocco.

cards.name: Mozambique
cards.story: Portugal held coastal slave-trading posts from 1505—trafficking hundreds of thousands of enslaved Africans—and secured Mozambique's colonial borders in the 1890s via forced labor and military subjugation. After a 10-year independence war (1964–74) killed tens of thousands, a brutal 1977–92 civil war backed by white-minority Rhodesia and apartheid South Africa killed roughly 1 million people—mostly through war-induced famine—and displaced over 5 million.

environment.biomeLabel: Indian Ocean Coast, Coral Reef & Miombo Savanna
environment.summary: Mozambique stretches along a long tropical coastline of mangrove estuaries and Bazaruto coral islands, rising inland to miombo woodlands and Zambezi River floodplains.

triviaItems.fact: The UNESCO-listed Gule Wamkulu masked dance of the Chewa people is a shared cultural tradition across Malawi, Zambia, and Mozambique.
Marrabenta guitar music and UNESCO-listed Chopi timbila xylophone orchestras originate in Mozambique.

cards.name: Myanmar
cards.story: Britain conquered Burma in three 19th-century wars and forcibly joined central Burman plains with autonomous ethnic borderlands under colonial rule until independence in 1948, igniting the world's longest-running civil wars. In August 2017, Myanmar's military launched genocidal 'clearance operations' in Rakhine State—killing thousands (at least 6,700 in the first month alone) and driving over 740,000 Rohingya refugees into Bangladesh (bringing total displaced Rohingya to ~1 million)—while the 2021 military coup triggered nationwide war displacing over 3.5 million more.
cards.contestedNote: UN investigators have documented genocide and crimes against humanity against the Rohingya (~1 million displaced in Bangladesh) alongside ongoing nationwide civil war following the 2021 military coup.

environment.biomeLabel: Monsoon River Basin, Forest & Himalayan Spur
environment.summary: The broad Irrawaddy valley and coastal mangrove deltas sit inside a horseshoe of forested Arakan, Shan, and snow-capped northern Kachin mountains.

triviaItems.fact: Thingyan, the traditional Burmese New Year water festival, and golden stupas like Shwedagon Pagoda are icons of Myanmar.

cards.name: Namibia
cards.story: Germany colonized Namibia in 1884 and, when the Herero and Nama peoples rose against land seizure and brutality in 1904–08, carried out the 20th century's first genocide—driving survivors into the desert and concentration camps and killing 65,000–80,000 Herero (about 80% of the population) and ~10,000 Nama (about 50%). Apartheid South Africa later occupied Namibia for decades, fighting a 23-year liberation war that killed over 20,000 before independence in 1990.

environment.summary: Namibia is defined by the towering red dunes of the Namib Desert, the fog-fed Skeleton Coast, Etosha salt pan, and dry inland acacia savannas.

triviaItems.fact: Red-ochre otjize body art of the Himba people and Herero Day processions in Okahandja are cultural traditions of Namibia.

cards.name: Nauru
cards.story: Colonized by Germany in 1888 and later governed by Australia, Britain, and New Zealand, Nauru's interior was strip-mined for phosphate for nearly a century, leaving roughly 80% of the island barren. During World War II, Japan occupied Nauru and forcibly deported 1,200 Nauruans—about two-thirds of the population—to forced labor on Chuuk, where ~463 died before survivors returned and won independence in 1968.

environment.summary: Nauru is a tiny oval phosphate-rich limestone island in Micronesia ringed by a coastal palm belt and a narrow fringing coral reef.

triviaItems.fact: Traditional frigatebird-taming competitions and Angam Day are cultural traditions of Nauru.

cards.name: Nepal
cards.story: Unified from Himalayan kingdoms by Prithvi Narayan Shah in 1768, Nepal was never colonized by Britain, though defeat in the 1814–16 Anglo-Nepalese War forced the Treaty of Sugauli, stripping roughly a third of its territory to British India. In modern times, the 1996–2006 Maoist civil war killed an estimated 17,000 people and displaced over 100,000 before abolishing the monarchy in 2008.

environment.summary: Within just 200 kilometers, Nepal rises from humid subtropical Terai plains and jungles through terraced mid-hills to eight of Earth's ten highest peaks.

triviaItems.fact: Deepawali—celebrated as the five-day Tihar festival of lights with oil lamps and marigold garlands—is one of Nepal's major annual holidays.
Siddhartha Gautama (the Buddha) was born in Nepal.
Mount Everest sits on the border of China and Nepal.

cards.name: Netherlands
cards.turningPoint: 1648 Peace of Westphalia & 1839 Treaty of London
cards.story: The Dutch Republic won independence from Spain in 1648 after an 80-year war, fixed its European borders in 1839, and endured brutal Nazi WWII occupation—during which ~102,000 Dutch Jews (75% of the community) were murdered in the Holocaust and ~20,000 died in the 1944–45 Hunger Winter. Overseas, the Dutch Empire trafficked roughly 550,000–600,000 enslaved Africans to Suriname and the Caribbean and waged bloody colonial wars in Indonesia killing hundreds of thousands.

environment.summary: The Netherlands sits on the low-lying delta of the Rhine, Meuse, and Scheldt rivers, shaped by coastal dunes, Wadden Sea mudflats, canals, and reclaimed polders.

triviaItems.fact: The Netherlands is famous for its tulip fields and historic windmills.
The Netherlands built more historic drainage and grain windmills than any other country.

cards.name: New Caledonia
cards.story: France annexed New Caledonia in 1853, turning it into a penal colony (~22,000 convicts sent) and seizing over 90% of fertile land from the Indigenous Kanak people—violently crushing Kanak uprisings in 1878 (~1,000+ Kanaks killed) and 1917 while confining survivors to reserves. Pro-independence clashes in the 1980s (including the 1988 Ouvéa cave assault) led to the 1998 Nouméa Accord, though tensions erupted again in 2024 killing over a dozen people.
cards.contestedNote: New Caledonia remains a special collectivity of France; Kanak self-determination movements contest France's constitutional framework, with renewed unrest breaking out in 2024.

environment.biomeLabel: Tropical Pacific Island & Barrier Reef Lagoon
environment.summary: New Caledonia centers on a rugged main island (Grande Terre) surrounded by one of Earth's largest coral reef lagoons, endemic pine forests, and the Loyalty Islands.

triviaItems.fact: The Jean-Marie Tjibaou Cultural Centre celebrating Kanak architecture and yam-harvest ceremonies is located in New Caledonia.

cards.name: New Zealand
cards.story: Settled by Polynesian Māori navigators centuries before European arrival, Aotearoa New Zealand entered British rule through the disputed 1840 Treaty of Waitangi. When Māori resisted settler land grabs, British and colonial armies fought the 1845–72 New Zealand Wars—killing ~2,000+ Māori fighters and civilians and confiscating roughly 3.5 million acres of ancestral Māori land—as disease and dispossession cut the Māori population by more than half before New Zealand became a self-governing dominion in 1907.

environment.summary: New Zealand comprises two dramatic Pacific islands pairing geothermal volcanic plateaus in the north with glacier-carved Southern Alps, fjords, and ancient beech rainforests.

triviaItems.fact: The All Blacks are the national rugby team of New Zealand.
The kiwi, a flightless bird, is the national symbol of New Zealand.
The Māori are the indigenous people of New Zealand.

cards.name: Nicaragua
cards.story: Spanish conquest and slave trading in the 1520s–40s decimated Nicaragua's Indigenous population by over 80% before independence from Spain (1821) and the Central American Federation (1838); Nicaragua forcibly incorporated the autonomous Miskito Coast in 1894. Following U.S. military occupations (1912–33) and the Somoza dictatorship, the 1978–79 Sandinista Revolution and U.S.-backed 1980s Contra War killed an estimated 50,000 to 80,000 Nicaraguans and displaced hundreds of thousands.

environment.summary: A line of active Pacific volcanoes borders immense freshwater Lake Nicaragua, while broad Caribbean lowlands hold dense Bosawás tropical rainforest.

triviaItems.fact: El Güegüense, a UNESCO-listed satirical street drama from colonial times, and the La Purísima festival are signature traditions of Nicaragua.

cards.name: Niger
cards.story: France conquered Niger in the 1890s through notoriously brutal military expeditions—including the 1899 Voulet-Chanoine mission that massacred thousands and razed entire villages—before drawing colonial borders with Britain that split Hausa and Tuareg homelands. Independent since 1960, recurring Tuareg rebellions and modern Sahel conflicts have displaced hundreds of thousands across its borders.

environment.summary: Niger is largely arid Saharan sand seas and the rugged volcanic Aïr massif, narrowing southward to semi-arid Sahel pastures and the fertile Niger River valley.

triviaItems.fact: The Wodaabe Gerewol courtship festival—shared across the Sahel with neighboring Chad—is a vibrant annual gathering in Niger.
The Cure Salée gathering of Tuareg and Wodaabe pastoralists at In-Gall takes place in Niger.

cards.name: Nigeria
cards.story: Britain conquered historic kingdoms including Benin (sacking and burning the city in 1897) and the Sokoto Caliphate, merging hundreds of ethnic nations into one colony in 1914 after centuries in which roughly 3.5 million enslaved Africans were trafficked from Nigeria's coasts. Seven years after independence in 1960, the Biafran Civil War (1967–70) and federal blockade killed an estimated 1 to 3 million people—predominantly children who starved—and displaced millions.

environment.summary: Nigeria progresses from vast Niger Delta mangroves and southern tropical forest through the Jos Plateau uplands to semi-arid northern Sahel grasslands.

triviaItems.fact: Fela Kuti, the pioneer of Afrobeat, was from Nigeria.
'Nollywood' is the film industry of Nigeria.

cards.name: North Korea
cards.story: Unified for over a millennium before brutal Japanese colonial occupation (1910–45)—which conscripted millions of Koreans into forced labor and sexual slavery—Korea was arbitrarily split at the 38th parallel by the U.S. and USSR in 1945. The 1950–53 Korean War devastated the peninsula, killing an estimated 3 to 4 million people (including 2 to 3 million civilians and heavy U.S. bombing that flattened northern cities), displacing roughly 3 million, and permanently separating millions of families across the DMZ.
cards.contestedNote: No peace treaty has ever replaced the 1953 armistice; the Demilitarized Zone remains one of the world's most heavily militarized borders, and both Koreas have historically claimed sovereignty over the entire peninsula.

environment.summary: Roughly 80% of North Korea consists of rugged forested mountains—including volcanic Mount Paektu—descending to western Yellow Sea plains and eastern Sea of Japan coasts.

triviaItems.fact: Chuseok (Hangawi), a traditional autumn harvest holiday honoring ancestors with crescent-shaped songpyeon rice cakes, is observed across North Korea.
The Korean Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) separates North Korea and South Korea along the 38th parallel.

cards.name: North Macedonia
cards.story: Partitioned among Serbia, Greece, and Bulgaria after the 1912–13 Balkan Wars—accompanied by mass village burnings and displacements—the northern Vardar region became a Yugoslav republic in 1945 (after Bulgarian Axis forces deported over 7,100 Macedonian Jews—98% of the community—to Treblinka in 1943). North Macedonia separated peacefully from Yugoslavia in 1991, navigated a 2001 insurgency that displaced ~170,000 people, and resolved its naming dispute with Greece in 2019.

environment.summary: Rugged forested mountain ranges surround the Vardar River valley and ancient tectonic freshwater lakes Ohrid and Prespa.

triviaItems.fact: The Ohrid Summer Festival hosts classical concerts beside ancient Lake Ohrid in North Macedonia.

cards.name: Norway
cards.story: After centuries under Danish and Swedish rule, Norwegians voted overwhelmingly in 1905 to dissolve the union with Sweden peacefully. During World War II, Nazi Germany invaded and occupied Norway (1940–45), deporting ~770 Norwegian Jews to Auschwitz and razing northern Finnmark in a scorched-earth retreat that forcibly evacuated ~50,000 civilians; domestically, Norway's century-long 'Norwegianization' policy forcibly assimilated Indigenous Sámi communities.

environment.biomeLabel: Subarctic Fjords, Alpine Plateaus & Boreal Forest
environment.summary: Norway is sculpted by deep glacier-carved Atlantic fjords, high mountain plateaus, spruce forests, and the Arctic Lofoten and Svalbard archipelagos.

triviaItems.fact: The Northern Lights (Aurora Borealis) are best seen in Norway.
Norway is famous for its fjords.

cards.name: Oman
cards.story: One of the Arab world's oldest states, Oman built an Indian Ocean maritime empire stretching to Zanzibar—heavily tied to the East African slave trade until Britain pressured its abolition in the late 1800s—while British political advisers exerted deep colonial influence. During the 1963–76 Dhofar Rebellion in southern Oman, British-backed Omani forces suppressed separatist fighters, killing several thousand before border treaties finalized modern desert frontiers.

environment.biomeLabel: Arabian Desert, Hajar Mountains & Monsoon Coast
environment.summary: Rugged Al Hajar limestone ranges and golden Wahiba sand dunes contrast with frankincense-growing southern Dhofar hills watered by summer khareef mists.

triviaItems.fact: Ancient Dhofar frankincense trade routes and traditional Omani khanjar daggers are cultural icons of Oman.

cards.name: Pakistan
cards.story: Created in August 1947 through Britain's abrupt Partition of India, Pakistan was born amid catastrophic communal violence that killed an estimated 500,000 to 2 million people and forcibly displaced 12 to 18 million across Punjab and Bengal. Originally split into West and East Pakistan separated by India, West Pakistan's brutal 1971 military crackdown in East Pakistan killed hundreds of thousands and drove ~10 million refugees into India before East Pakistan broke away as Bangladesh.
cards.contestedNote: Pakistan and India have fought multiple wars over disputed Kashmir since 1947, divided today along the militarized Line of Control, while Afghanistan has never formally recognized the 1893 colonial Durand Line.

environment.biomeLabel: Karakoram Peaks, Indus Plains & Baluchistan Desert
environment.summary: Pakistan unites glaciated Karakoram and Himalayan giants—including K2—with fertile irrigated Indus River plains, dry Balochistan plateaus, and Arabian Sea mangroves.

cards.name: Palau
cards.story: Colonized in turn by Spain, Germany, and Japan—under whom epidemics and colonial displacement shrank the Palauan population before World War II's bloody 1944 Battle of Peleliu killed over 12,000 Japanese and U.S. troops and forced Palauans to evacuate—Palau entered a U.S.-run UN Trust Territory. Choosing its own nuclear-free constitution, Palau became fully independent in 1994.

environment.biomeLabel: Tropical Limestone Rock Islands & Coral Reef
environment.summary: Palau features hundreds of emerald mushroom-shaped limestone Rock Islands, marine lakes, rainforest hills, and western Pacific barrier reefs.

triviaItems.fact: Painted wooden bai meeting houses with carved storyboard legends and marine Jellyfish Lake are iconic sights of Palau.

cards.name: Palestine
cards.story: Following the Ottoman Empire's collapse, Britain governed Palestine under a League of Nations mandate until 1948, crushing the 1936–39 Arab Revolt (killing ~5,000 Palestinians). The 1948 war and establishment of Israel triggered the Nakba—forcibly displacing over 700,000 Palestinians and destroying over 400 villages—leaving the West Bank under Jordanian rule and Gaza under Egyptian administration until Israel's 1967 military conquest placed both under occupation and displaced roughly 300,000 more Palestinians; Palestine declared independence in 1988 and became a UN Observer State in 2012.
cards.contestedNote: Recognized as a state by over 140 UN members, Palestine remains under Israeli military occupation, illegal West Bank settlement expansion, and blockade. Since October 2023, Israel's military assault on Gaza—widely described by UN experts and human rights organizations as genocide—has killed over 70,000 Palestinians and displaced the vast majority of Gaza's 2.2 million residents.

environment.biomeLabel: Mediterranean Hills, Jordan Valley & Coastal Plain
environment.summary: Palestine combines the terraced olive-clad limestone highlands of the West Bank, descending toward the Jordan Valley and Dead Sea, with the sandy Mediterranean plain of Gaza.

triviaItems.fact: Palestine borders the Dead Sea, Earth's lowest point on land.

cards.name: Panama
cards.story: Spanish conquest decimated Indigenous populations across the isthmus and turned Panama into a transit hub for enslaved Africans and looted Peruvian silver before it became part of Colombia. Backed by U.S. gunboats seeking a canal route, Panama broke from Colombia in 1903—building the Panama Canal at the cost of over 25,000 worker deaths (mostly Afro-Caribbean laborers)—and endured a 1989 U.S. invasion (killing hundreds of civilians) before regaining full control of the Canal Zone in 1999.

environment.summary: Panama forms a narrow mountainous land bridge cloaked in Darién and cloud rainforests linking Caribbean coral islands with Pacific mangrove bays.

triviaItems.fact: The Panama Canal connects the Atlantic and Pacific oceans through Panama.

cards.name: Papua New Guinea
cards.story: European empires sliced New Guinea down the 141st meridian in the 1880s—Britain and Germany seizing the eastern half (with German colonial plantations using coerced labor and killing hundreds in punitive raids) before Australia took control after World War I; World War II's brutal New Guinea campaign killed over 200,000 Japanese and Allied troops and tens of thousands of Papua New Guineans. Independent since 1975, a 1988–98 civil war and blockade on Bougainville killed an estimated 15,000 to 20,000 people and displaced ~60,000.

environment.summary: Steep cloud-wrapped Owen Stanley and Bismarck mountain spines divide vast lowland swamp jungles, active volcanic arcs, and Coral Sea reefs.

triviaItems.fact: Papua New Guinea is known as the 'Land of the Unexpected'.

cards.name: Paraguay
cards.story: After Spanish colonial missions and conquest reshaped Guaraní lands, Paraguay declared independence in 1811—only to be nearly destroyed in the 1864–70 War of the Triple Alliance against Brazil, Argentina, and Uruguay, which stripped vast territory and killed an estimated 50% to 69% of Paraguay's pre-war population through combat, famine, and disease. A 1932–35 Chaco War with Bolivia killed ~36,000 more Paraguayans before a 1938 treaty secured the Gran Chaco.

environment.summary: Paraguay is divided by the Paraguay River between the semi-arid thorny savannas of the western Gran Chaco and fertile rolling eastern subtropical hills.

triviaItems.fact: Intricate Ñandutí spiderweb lace and the 36-string Paraguayan harp are UNESCO-recognized cultural traditions of Paraguay.

cards.name: Peru
cards.story: Spain's 1532–72 conquest of the Inca Empire—alongside Old World epidemics and brutal forced mita labor in silver and mercury mines—collapsed Peru's Indigenous population from ~9–12 million to under 1 million, while colonial Peru also imported ~100,000 enslaved Africans before independence in 1821 and territorial losses to Chile in 1879–84. Between 1980 and 2000, internal war between Shining Path insurgents and state forces killed an estimated 69,000 Peruvians—75% of them Indigenous Quechua speakers—and displaced ~600,000.

environment.biomeLabel: Pacific Coastal Desert, Andes & Amazon Basin
environment.summary: Peru divides sharply into an arid Pacific coastal strip, towering glacier-capped Andean cordilleras, high Lake Titicaca, and sprawling lowland Amazonian jungle.

triviaItems.fact: Inti Raymi, the Inca winter-solstice Festival of the Sun recreated each June in Cusco, is celebrated in Peru.
The ancient Inca citadel of Machu Picchu is in Peru.
The mysterious Nazca Lines are located in Peru.
Llamas and alpacas were first domesticated in Peru.

cards.name: Philippines
cards.story: Spain colonized over 7,000 islands starting in the 1560s—imposing forced labor and crushing Indigenous and Moro resistance—before ceding the archipelago to the United States in 1898 despite a Filipino independence revolution. In the brutal 1899–1902 Philippine–American War, U.S. forces used reconcentration camps and scorched-earth tactics that killed an estimated 20,000 Filipino fighters and 200,000 to 250,000 civilians (mostly through war-induced famine and cholera); World War II's Japanese occupation and Battle of Manila later killed ~500,000 to 1 million Filipinos before independence in 1946.

environment.summary: The Philippines spans over 7,600 Ring of Fire islands combining volcanic cones, karst Palawan lagoons, terraced mountain highlands, and Coral Triangle reefs.

cards.name: Poland
cards.story: Partitioned off the map by Russia, Prussia, and Austria in 1795 and reborn in 1918, Poland was invaded simultaneously by Nazi Germany and the USSR in 1939. During World War II, roughly 5.6 to 6 million Polish citizens—nearly 17% of the entire nation, including ~3 million Polish Jews (90% of Poland's Jewish population)—were murdered, and the 1945 Potsdam borders shifted Poland ~150 miles west, forcibly uprooting ~1.5 to 2 million Poles from Soviet-annexed eastern lands and expelling millions of Germans from the west.

environment.summary: Wide glacial plains, Masurian lake districts, and ancient Białowieża woodland rise southward to the rocky alpine ridges of the Tatra Mountains.

triviaItems.fact: Midsummer solstice celebrations (Noc Kupały) with bonfires and floating flower wreaths are a beloved folk tradition in Poland.
The Solidarity movement that helped end communism began in Poland.

cards.name: Portugal
cards.story: Portugal's mainland borders with Spain have barely changed since the 1297 Treaty of Alcañices following the Reconquista—which also led to the 1496–97 forced conversion and expulsion of tens of thousands of Jews and Muslims. Overseas, Portugal pioneered the transatlantic slave trade—trafficking roughly 5.8 million enslaved Africans (nearly half the entire trade, mostly to Brazil)—and waged brutal 1961–74 colonial wars in Angola, Mozambique, and Guinea-Bissau that killed over 100,000 before Portugal's 1974 Carnation Revolution ended its empire.

environment.biomeLabel: Atlantic Coast, Cork Woodland & Mediterranean South
environment.summary: Lush green northern hills and terraced Douro river valleys give way to sunlit Alentejo cork-oak plains, Algarve sea cliffs, and volcanic Atlantic islands.

triviaItems.fact: Fado, the soulful UNESCO-listed musical tradition of Lisbon and Coimbra, originated in Portugal.

cards.name: Qatar
cards.story: Consolidating under the Al Thani family in the 1800s, Qatar signed a 1916 British protectorate treaty granting Britain control over its foreign affairs and defense in exchange for maritime protection. When Britain ended its Gulf protectorates in 1971, Qatar chose independent statehood and settled its remaining land and maritime border disputes with Bahrain and Saudi Arabia by 2001.

environment.summary: Qatar is a flat limestone-and-sand desert peninsula jutting into the Persian Gulf, edged by salty sabkha flats, Khor Al Adaid inland dunes, and coastal mangroves.

triviaItems.fact: Historic Souq Waqif in Doha, traditional falconry, and pearl-diving maritime songs are cultural traditions of Qatar.

cards.name: Republic of the Congo
cards.story: At the 1884–85 Berlin Conference, France claimed the northwestern Congo River basin and handed vast tracts to ruthless concession companies; building the colonial Congo-Océan Railway (1921–34) through forced labor killed an estimated 15,000 to 20,000 African conscripts. Independent since 1960, civil wars in the 1990s killed tens of thousands and displaced over 800,000 civilians.

environment.summary: More than two-thirds of the Republic of the Congo is draped in dense equatorial rainforest and Cuvette Centrale peatlands draining into the Congo River and Atlantic coast.

triviaItems.fact: Congolese Rumba (inscribed by UNESCO) and Brazzaville's Pan-African Music Festival (FESPAM) are celebrated in the Republic of the Congo.
The UNESCO-listed vocal polyphony of the Aka forest peoples is a living musical heritage of the Republic of the Congo.

cards.name: Romania
cards.story: United from Wallachia and Moldavia in 1859 and expanded in 1918 to include Transylvania, Romania lost Bessarabia and northern Bukovina to the USSR in 1940–44, fixing today's borders. During World War II, Romania's fascist Antonescu regime and German allies murdered an estimated 280,000 to 380,000 Jews and ~11,000 Roma across Romania, Bessarabia, and Transnistria, while post-war Soviet rule deported tens of thousands of ethnic Germans and political prisoners to forced labor.

environment.biomeLabel: Carpathian Mountain Arc, Plains & Danube Delta
environment.summary: A sweeping horseshoe of forested Carpathian Mountains encloses Transylvanian hills, draining outward into fertile plains and Europe's richest wetland, the Danube Delta.

triviaItems.fact: The legend of Dracula originates from Romania.

cards.name: Russia
cards.story: Expanding from Muscovy across Siberia, the Caucasus, and Central Asia through imperial conquest—including the 1864 Circassian genocide (killing ~400,000–600,000+ and expelling 700,000–1 million Circassians)—Russia formed the core of the USSR, which endured Stalinist purges, forced deportations of millions, and ~26–27 million Soviet deaths in World War II before dissolving in 1991. Since 1991, Russia's two Chechen wars killed an estimated 100,000–200,000+ (mostly civilians), and its 2014 and 2022 invasions of Ukraine have caused hundreds of thousands of casualties and displaced nearly 10 million Ukrainians.
cards.contestedNote: Russia's internationally recognized 1991 borders do not include Crimea or four eastern/southern Ukrainian regions Russia has militarily occupied and illegally claimed since 2014 and 2022.

environment.biomeLabel: Boreal Taiga, Arctic Tundra & Eurasian Steppe
environment.summary: Earth's largest country spans frozen Arctic tundra, vast Siberian coniferous taiga, southern grasslands, Caucasus peaks, volcanic Kamchatka, and deepest Lake Baikal.

triviaItems.fact: Maslenitsa (Butter Week), celebrated with golden blini pancakes to welcome spring, is a traditional festival of Russia.

cards.name: Rwanda
cards.story: Colonized by Germany in the 1890s and Belgium after World War I, Rwanda's pre-colonial kingdom was fractured by Belgian colonial identity cards and racialized policies that entrenched Hutu–Tutsi divisions before independence in 1962—preceded by 1959–61 pogroms that drove over 130,000 Tutsis into exile. In 1994, extremist leaders orchestrated the Rwandan Genocide, murdering an estimated 500,000 to 800,000+ people (mostly Tutsis) in 100 days and displacing roughly 3 million internally and across borders.

environment.biomeLabel: East African Montane Rainforest & Volcanic Hills
environment.summary: The Land of a Thousand Hills pairs steep terraced highlands and Lake Kivu shores with misty Virunga volcanic bamboo forests and eastern Akagera savannas.

triviaItems.fact: Endangered mountain gorillas live in volcanic forests of Rwanda.
Volcanoes National Park, famous for mountain gorilla trekking, is in Rwanda.

cards.name: Samoa
cards.story: An 1899 imperial treaty split Samoa without Samoan consent—handing eastern islands to the United States and western islands to Germany and then New Zealand after World War I. In 1918, New Zealand colonial negligence allowed the Spanish flu ashore, killing roughly 8,500 Samoans (~22% of the entire population), and NZ police shot dead ~11 peaceful Mau independence demonstrators on 'Black Saturday' in 1929 before Samoa became the first Pacific nation to regain independence in 1962.

environment.summary: Samoa comprises the lush emerald volcanic islands of Upolu and Savai'i, featuring cloud-forest craters, lava fields, cascading waterfalls, and turquoise fringing reefs.

triviaItems.fact: The Teuila Cultural Festival, Fa'a Sāmoa communal life, and traditional pe'a tattooing (tatau) are central pillars of Samoan culture.

cards.name: San Marino
cards.story: Founded around 301 CE on Mount Titano, San Marino is among the world's oldest surviving republics, with borders unchanged since 1463 and respected during Italian unification in the 1860s. Though neutral during World War II, it sheltered roughly 100,000 Italian war refugees—more than six times its own population—even after an Allied bombing raid accidentally killed 63 residents in 1944.

environment.summary: San Marino is crowned by the three-peaked limestone outcrop of Mount Titano overlooking rolling Adriatic foothills and Mediterranean oak-and-olive slopes.

triviaItems.fact: The Medieval Days festival celebrates Europe's oldest surviving republic atop Mount Titano in San Marino.

cards.name: São Tomé & Príncipe
cards.story: Uninhabited until Portuguese colonizers arrived in the 1470s, São Tomé and Príncipe became Europe's earliest tropical slave-plantation colony—pioneering the forced African labor model later exported to the Americas—and later relied on coerced Angolan and Cabo Verdean contract laborers. After colonial troops killed hundreds of striking islanders in the 1953 Batepá Massacre, the islands won independence in 1975.

environment.summary: São Tomé and Príncipe consists of two lush volcanic islands in the Gulf of Guinea featuring dramatic rock spires like Pico Cão Grande, mist forests, and coastal cocoa groves.

triviaItems.fact: Tchiloli, a centuries-old open-air folk drama blending Renaissance theater with African percussion, is performed in São Tomé & Príncipe.

cards.name: Saudi Arabia
cards.story: Starting in 1902, Abdulaziz Ibn Saud and his Ikhwan fighters waged decades of military campaigns across Arabia—conquering Najd, Al-Hasa, Hail, and the Hejaz (home to Mecca and Medina) in wars that killed tens of thousands—to proclaim Saudi Arabia in 1932, with British-drawn colonial treaties setting its northern borders. Since 2015, Saudi Arabia's military coalition intervention and blockade in neighboring Yemen's civil war has contributed to a humanitarian crisis linked to ~377,000 deaths and millions displaced.

environment.biomeLabel: Arabian Desert, Lava Fields & Red Sea Reef
environment.summary: Saudi Arabia is dominated by the immense Rub' al Khali sand desert and central Najd plateau, bordered by Hejaz-Asir escarpments and Red Sea coral reefs.

triviaItems.fact: The holy city of Mecca is in Saudi Arabia.
Saudi Arabia has the region's largest proven oil reserves.
OPEC was co-founded by Iran, Iraq, Kuwait, Venezuela, and Saudi Arabia.

cards.name: Senegal
cards.story: Gorée Island and Senegal's coast served as early gateways for European empires trafficking hundreds of thousands of enslaved Africans before France conquered interior kingdoms like Cayor and Jolof in the late 1800s. Colonial borders wrapped around British-held Gambia; Senegal gained independence in 1960, though a long-running separatist conflict in southern Casamance since 1982 has killed thousands and displaced tens of thousands.

environment.summary: Dry baobab savannas and the sweeping Senegal River delta give way southward to humid palm-lined rivers and mangroves in the Casamance.

triviaItems.fact: Sabar drumming, mbalax music, and the Saint-Louis International Jazz Festival are cultural signatures of Senegal.
The 21-string kora harp and griot (jali) oral storytelling are deeply rooted musical traditions of Senegal.

cards.name: Serbia
cards.story: Winning independence from Ottoman rule in the 1800s, Serbia suffered catastrophic losses in World War I (roughly 1.1 million dead—nearly a quarter of its population) and World War II before centering socialist Yugoslavia. During Yugoslavia's violent 1990s breakup, Serbian and Yugoslav forces led ethnic cleansing campaigns across Bosnia, Croatia, and Kosovo—while over 500,000 ethnic Serb refugees fled into Serbia from Croatia, Bosnia, and Kosovo—before Montenegro's 2006 split left Serbia's current borders.
cards.contestedNote: Serbia claims Kosovo as an autonomous province, whereas Kosovo declared independence in 2008 following the 1998–99 war and ethnic cleansing and is recognized by over 100 countries.

environment.biomeLabel: Pannonian Plain, Danube Gorge & Balkan Hills
environment.summary: Fertile flat Vojvodina farmlands along the Danube and Sava rivers rise southward into forested hills, karst gorges like the Iron Gates, and Kopaonik peaks.

triviaItems.fact: The Guča Trumpet Festival, one of Europe's largest brass-band gatherings, takes place in Serbia.

cards.name: Seychelles
cards.story: Uninhabited before French colonization in 1770 and British takeover in 1814, Seychelles was populated primarily by enslaved Africans brought to work colonial coconut and spice plantations—later joined by thousands of 'liberated Africans' intercepted from slave ships and placed into British indentured apprenticeship. The archipelago gained independence from Britain in 1976.

environment.summary: The Seychelles combines ancient granite islands draped in endemic coco-de-mer palm forests and boulder-strewn beaches with remote coral atolls like Aldabra.

triviaItems.fact: The UNESCO-listed Moutya bonfire dance and the Festival Kreol in Victoria are celebrated in the Seychelles.

cards.name: Sierra Leone
cards.story: After centuries in which hundreds of thousands of enslaved Africans were trafficked from Bunce Island and its coast, Britain established Freetown in 1787 for freed Black settlers and violently subjugated inland chiefdoms in 1896—crushing the 1898 Hut Tax War—before granting independence in 1961. A devastating 1991–2002 civil war fueled by conflict diamonds killed an estimated 50,000 to 70,000 people and displaced over 2 million—nearly half the population.

environment.summary: Lush mountainous Freetown Peninsula beaches and coastal mangrove swamps transition inland to wooded hills, tropical rainforest reserves, and Loma peaks.

triviaItems.fact: Freetown's annual Lantern Parade of illuminated bamboo floats and Krio heritage are cultural traditions of Sierra Leone.

cards.name: Singapore
cards.story: Britain seized Singapore in 1819 as a colonial trading outpost, building its port on migrant Chinese, Malay, and Indian labor. During World War II, Japan's 1942–45 occupation carried out the Sook Ching massacres, executing an estimated 25,000 to 50,000 ethnic Chinese civilians across Singapore and Malaya; after briefly joining Malaysia in 1963, political and ethnic tensions led to Singapore's separation as an independent city-state in 1965.

environment.summary: Singapore is a warm, humid island at the tip of the Malay Peninsula that preserves pockets of Bukit Timah rainforest, Sungei Buloh mangroves, and tropical gardens.

triviaItems.fact: UNESCO-listed Hawker Centre street-food culture, uniting Chinese, Malay, and Indian cuisines, is a signature of Singapore.

cards.name: Slovakia
cards.story: Ruled within the Kingdom of Hungary for nearly a millennium, Slovak lands joined Czechoslovakia in 1918. As a Nazi-allied puppet state during World War II (1939–45), Slovakia's regime deported roughly 70,000 Slovak Jews to Nazi death camps—with ~68,000 murdered in the Holocaust—before reuniting with Czechoslovakia after WWII, expelling ethnic Germans and Hungarians, and peacefully separating from the Czech Republic in 1993.

environment.summary: Slovakia is dominated by the granite High Tatras and forested Carpathian ranges, descending to fertile Danube lowlands in the southwest.

triviaItems.fact: The Východná Folklore Festival celebrates Carpathian folk dance and fujara flute music in Slovakia.

cards.name: Slovenia
cards.story: Ruled for centuries by the Habsburg Empire before joining Yugoslavia in 1918, Slovenia endured brutal Axis partition during World War II—when Nazi Germany forcibly deported ~60,000 Slovenes and Fascist Italy interned ~25,000 in concentration camps—followed by post-war Yugoslav executions of ~15,000 anti-communist prisoners. Slovenia declared independence in June 1991 and secured its modern borders after a brief ten-day war.

environment.biomeLabel: Julian Alps, Karst Caves & Adriatic Coast
environment.summary: Slovenia packs snow-capped Julian Alps, emerald glacial lakes, subterranean limestone karst caves, dense forests, and a sunny Adriatic coast into a compact landscape.

triviaItems.fact: Kurentovanje, a UNESCO-listed carnival of sheepskin-clad Kurenti chasing away winter in Ptuj, takes place in Slovenia.

cards.name: Solomon Islands
cards.story: Before Britain declared a protectorate in 1893, 19th-century Pacific 'blackbirding' labor traffickers kidnapped or coerced roughly 30,000 Solomon Islanders to work plantations in Queensland and Fiji, and British punitive raids crushed local resistance (including the 1927 Malaita massacre). World War II's fierce Guadalcanal campaign killed over 30,000 Japanese and Allied troops before independence in 1978; later ethnic tensions (1998–2003) displaced over 20,000 islanders.

environment.summary: The Solomon Islands spans nearly a thousand mountainous volcanic islands and coral atolls covered in dense tropical rainforest and clear Melanesian lagoons.

triviaItems.fact: Ensemble bamboo panpipe orchestras and intricate shell-inlay woodcarving are signature cultural arts of the Solomon Islands.

cards.name: Somalia
cards.story: During the Scramble for Africa, Britain, Italy, France, and Ethiopia partitioned Somali-speaking lands across five territories, crushing Dervish anti-colonial resistance with Britain's first aerial bombing campaign in Africa in 1920. British and Italian Somaliland united upon independence in 1960, but a 1988–91 regime crackdown in the north killed an estimated 50,000 to 200,000 Isaaq civilians (prompting Somaliland's breakaway), and decades of civil war and famine since 1991 have killed over 500,000 people and displaced over 3.8 million.
cards.contestedNote: Northern Somaliland declared independence in 1991 after state massacres killed tens of thousands of Isaaq civilians; it governs itself separately while remaining internationally recognized as part of Somalia.

environment.biomeLabel: Arid Horn of Africa Scrub & Indian Ocean Coast
environment.summary: Africa's longest mainland coastline backs semi-arid acacia plains, northern Cal Madow mountain escarpments, and fertile southern Jubba and Shabelle river valleys.

triviaItems.fact: Somalia is celebrated as the 'Nation of Poets' for its rich oral gabay verse and traditional Dhaanto dance.

cards.name: South Africa
cards.story: Dutch and British colonial conquest dispossessed Khoisan, Xhosa, Zulu, and other African societies through frontier wars and the 1899–1902 South African War—where British concentration camps killed over 26,000 Boer civilians and at least 14,000–20,000 Black Africans—before Britain united four colonies under white-minority rule in 1910. Under Apartheid (1948–94), the regime forcibly uprooted roughly 3.5 million Black, Coloured, and Indian South Africans into segregated townships and 'homelands' and killed thousands of anti-apartheid activists before 1994 multiracial democracy ended the system.

environment.summary: South Africa bridges two oceans across extraordinary biomes, including floral Cape Fynbos, the semi-desert Karoo, towering Drakensberg escarpments, and Kruger savanna.

triviaItems.fact: South Africa ended apartheid in 1994.
Nelson Mandela was president of South Africa.

cards.name: South Korea
cards.story: After thirty-five years of harsh Japanese colonial occupation (1910–45) that mobilized millions of Koreans for forced labor and military sexual slavery, Allied powers arbitrarily split Korea at the 38th parallel. The 1950–53 Korean War killed an estimated 3 to 4 million people (including 2 to 3 million Korean civilians, alongside wartime massacres such as Jeju 4.3 and Bodo League), displaced roughly 3 million, and froze the peninsula behind the Demilitarized Zone.
cards.contestedNote: The Demilitarized Zone separates South and North Korea under the 1953 armistice rather than a permanent peace treaty, keeping millions of separated family lineages divided.

environment.summary: Forested Taebaek and Sobaek mountain spines descend to fertile western river basins, tidal mudflats, and volcanic Jeju Island to the south.

triviaItems.fact: Chuseok, a major autumn harvest festival featuring songpyeon rice cakes and ancestral rites, is celebrated in South Korea.
Kimchi is a traditional food of South Korea.
K-pop music originates from South Korea.
The Korean Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) separates North Korea and South Korea along the 38th parallel.

cards.name: South Sudan
cards.story: Britain governed northern and southern Sudan separately under colonial rule before merging them at independence in 1956, igniting two brutal civil wars (1955–72 and 1983–2005) that killed an estimated 2 million people—mostly southern civilians from fighting and war-induced famine—and displaced over 4 million. Nearly 99% of southern voters chose independence in 2011, yet a post-independence civil war (2013–18) killed an estimated 380,000–400,000 more and displaced over 4 million.
cards.contestedNote: Several border zones with Sudan, especially the oil-rich Abyei area, remain disputed and await final demarcation.

environment.summary: South Sudan centers on the Sudd—one of Earth's largest seasonal freshwater wetlands fed by the White Nile—surrounded by wide grasslands and the southern Imatong peaks.

triviaItems.fact: Traditional Dinka and Mundari wrestling tournaments and cattle-camp songs are central cultural gatherings in South Sudan.

cards.name: Spain
cards.story: Forged by the 1469 union of Castile and Aragon and the 1492 conquest of Granada—followed by the expulsion of ~100,000–200,000 Jews (1492) and ~300,000 Moriscos (1609)—Spain fixed its French border in 1659, ceded Gibraltar to Britain in the 1713 Treaty of Utrecht, and annexed Olivenza from Portugal in 1801 while building an American empire whose conquests, forced labor, and epidemics drove an 80–90% Indigenous population collapse alongside trafficking ~1 million enslaved Africans. Domestically, the 1936–39 Spanish Civil War and Franco's dictatorship killed roughly 500,000 people and forced ~450,000–500,000 Republicans into exile.

environment.summary: Spain centers on a sun-warmed central plateau ringed by the snowy Pyrenees and Sierra Nevada, contrasting misty green Atlantic Galicia with arid southeastern hills.

triviaItems.fact: The annual La Tomatina tomato-throwing festival is celebrated in Buñol in Spain.
Flamenco dance originated in Spain.
Tapas culture originates from Spain.

cards.name: Sri Lanka
cards.story: Conquered successively by Portuguese, Dutch, and British empires by 1815—with British troops crushing the 1817–18 Uva Rebellion through scorched-earth tactics killing ~10,000—Ceylon won independence in 1948 and became Sri Lanka in 1972. Post-independence state discrimination against the Tamil minority sparked anti-Tamil pogroms (notably Black July 1983) and a 26-year civil war (1983–2009) that killed an estimated 70,000 to 100,000+ people—including 40,000 to 70,000 civilians in the brutal 2009 final offensive—and displaced hundreds of thousands.

environment.summary: Sri Lanka is a tear-shaped Indian Ocean island rising from palm-lined beaches and dry northern plains to cool tea-clad central highlands and Sinharaja rainforest.

triviaItems.fact: Deepavali (Diwali), the five-day Festival of Lights celebrated with clay oil lamps and rangoli, is widely celebrated across Sri Lanka.
Sri Lanka is one of the world's largest tea exporters.

cards.name: St. Kitts & Nevis
cards.story: In 1626, English and French colonizers jointly massacred an estimated 2,000 Indigenous Kalinago people at Bloody Point on St. Kitts to establish their first permanent Caribbean colonies. Over the next two centuries, colonizers trafficked over 140,000 enslaved Africans onto St. Kitts and Nevis sugar plantations before the twin-island federation achieved independence in 1983.

environment.summary: Steep cloud-capped volcanic cones of Mount Liamuiga and Nevis Peak descend through lush rainforest ravines to sandy Caribbean coastlines.

triviaItems.fact: Sugar Mas, a winter Carnival rooted in sugar-plantation folklore and moko jumbie stilt walkers, is celebrated in St. Kitts & Nevis.

cards.name: St. Lucia
cards.story: Indigenous Kalinago defenders fought off early European settlements for decades before France and Britain waged wars over St. Lucia, changing hands fourteen times while trafficking tens of thousands of enslaved Africans to its plantations until Britain took permanent control in 1814. St. Lucia won full independence from Britain in 1979.

environment.summary: Saint Lucia features dramatic twin volcanic spires (the Pitons), sulphur springs, dense mountain rainforests, and sheltered emerald bays in the Windward Islands.

triviaItems.fact: The Saint Lucia Jazz & Arts Festival and twin volcanic Piton peaks are icons of St. Lucia.

cards.name: St. Vincent & the Grenadines
cards.story: Indigenous Kalinago and Afro-Indigenous Garifuna communities fiercely resisted British colonial invasion through two Carib Wars until Britain defeated them in 1796–97, detaining ~5,000 Garifuna on Baliceaux Island—where roughly half died of starvation and disease—before forcibly deporting survivors to Central America and expanding African plantation slavery. The islands gained independence in 1979.

environment.summary: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines pairs lush, steep volcanic St. Vincent—crowned by active La Soufrière—with thirty-two coral cays and turquoise Tobago Cays reefs.

triviaItems.fact: Vincy Mas Carnival and the Nine Mornings pre-dawn Christmas street festival are traditions of St. Vincent & the Grenadines.

cards.name: Sudan
cards.story: Britain and Egypt conquered Sudan in 1898—killing over 10,000 Sudanese fighters in a single day at Omdurman—and drew colonial borders combining disparate regions until independence in 1956, fueling decades of north-south civil war that killed ~2 million before South Sudan seceded in 2011. In Darfur (2003–08), state forces and Janjaweed militias committed genocide killing an estimated 200,000–300,000 people and displacing ~2.7 million; since April 2023, a new civil war has created the world's largest displacement crisis, forcing roughly 14 million people from their homes amid renewed massacres and famine.
cards.contestedNote: Sudan has unresolved border disputes with Egypt (the Hala'ib Triangle) and South Sudan (Abyei), while its ongoing civil war since 2023 has displaced roughly 14 million people and devastated Darfur and Khartoum.

environment.summary: Vast Nubian and Bayuda desert plains meet the dramatic confluence of the Blue and White Nile at Khartoum, transitioning southward to acacia savannas.

triviaItems.fact: The ancient Nubian pyramids of Meroë—more numerous than Egypt's—stand in Sudan.

cards.name: Suriname
cards.story: Traded by England to the Netherlands in 1667 for New Amsterdam (New York), Suriname became one of the Americas' harshest slave colonies—trafficking over 250,000 enslaved Africans while escaped Maroon communities fought decades of guerrilla wars for autonomy—followed by tens of thousands of Indian and Javanese indentured workers. Suriname gained independence in 1975, though a 1986–92 civil war killed hundreds (including the Moiwana Massacre) and displaced ~10,000–15,000 Maroons.

environment.summary: As Earth's most forested country, more than 90% of Suriname is blanketed in dense Amazonian rainforest veined by northward-flowing rivers and coastal wetlands.

triviaItems.fact: Suriname is the smallest sovereign country on the South American mainland.

cards.name: Sweden
cards.story: Once a dominant Baltic empire, Sweden lost Finland to Russia in 1809 and peacefully dissolved its union with Norway in 1905, maintaining unbroken peace since 1814 while sheltering tens of thousands of Nordic and Jewish refugees during World War II. Within its northern borders, however, centuries of Swedish state colonization of Sápmi displaced Indigenous Sámi reindeer herders and imposed forced residential schooling.

environment.summary: Sweden stretches from fertile southern farmlands and coastal archipelagos through pine-and-spruce lake country up to the snowy Arctic Scandinavian Mountains.

triviaItems.fact: ABBA formed in Sweden.
The Northern Lights (Aurora Borealis) are best seen in Sweden.
IKEA was founded in Sweden in 1943.

cards.name: Switzerland
cards.story: Born in 1291 as an Alpine mutual-defense pact, Switzerland grew into a 26-canton confederation whose modern borders and permanent neutrality were ratified at the 1815 Congress of Vienna after Napoleonic wars. During World War II, Switzerland remained unoccupied and took in ~50,000 civilian refugees (including ~21,000 Jews), though strict border policies turned away roughly 20,000–25,000 fleeing refugees—many of whom were deported to Nazi camps.

environment.summary: Switzerland is sculpted by snow-capped Alps and forested Jura ridges framing deep glacial lakes like Geneva and Lucerne alongside lush central meadows.

triviaItems.fact: Switzerland is world-famous for its artisanal chocolate and precision watchmaking.

cards.name: Syria
cards.turningPoint: 1920 San Remo Mandate, 1946 Independence & 2024 Regime Fall
cards.story: Carved from Ottoman provinces and assigned to French colonial mandate at the 1920 San Remo Conference (modifying the secret 1916 Sykes–Picot framework), Syria saw France crush the 1925–27 Great Syrian Revolt by shelling Damascus (~6,000 Syrians killed) and cede the Hatay province to Turkey in 1939 before independence in 1946; Israel seized the Golan Heights in 1967, displacing ~130,000 Syrians. Beginning in 2011, the Syrian Civil War and regime atrocities killed an estimated 500,000 to 600,000+ people and forcibly displaced over 12 million before Bashar al-Assad's 53-year family regime collapsed on December 8, 2024, leading to a transitional government.
cards.contestedNote: Israel has militarily occupied the Golan Heights since 1967 (displacing ~130,000 Syrians) and expanded buffer-zone operations in 2024; the international community considers the Golan occupied Syrian territory.

environment.summary: A narrow fertile coastal strip and mountain range give way eastward to rolling agricultural plains, the Euphrates valley, and the arid Syrian Desert.

triviaItems.fact: Damask silk weaving, inlaid marquetry, and the historic Umayyad Mosque of Damascus are enduring cultural treasures of Syria.

cards.name: Taiwan
cards.story: Home to Indigenous Austronesian peoples who suffered centuries of land dispossession and armed suppression under Qing rule and Japan's 50-year colonial occupation (1895–1945, including the 1930 Wushe massacre), Taiwan became the seat of the Republic of China in 1949 after the Chinese Civil War. Before democratizing, Kuomintang forces carried out the 1947 February 28 Massacre—killing an estimated 18,000 to 28,000 civilians—and imposed 38 years of White Terror martial law, arresting ~140,000 people.
cards.contestedNote: Taiwan operates as a self-governing democracy, while Beijing claims it as a province of China and threatens military force against formal independence.

environment.summary: Steep forest-cloaked Central Mountain Range peaks—rising nearly 4,000 meters—plunge to marble Taroko gorges in the east and fertile western plains.

triviaItems.fact: The Pingxi Sky Lantern Festival and vibrant night markets are celebrated cultural traditions of Taiwan.

cards.name: Tajikistan
cards.story: Conquered by the Russian Empire in the 1800s, Tajikistan's intricate mountain borders—splitting Tajik and Uzbek communities across the Fergana Valley—were drawn by Soviet boundary commissions in the 1920s after Red Army forces crushed the Basmachi anti-Soviet uprising. Just months after Soviet dissolution brought independence in 1991, the 1992–97 Tajik Civil War killed an estimated 50,000 to 100,000 people and displaced roughly 1.2 million—about one-fifth of the population.

environment.summary: More than 93% of Tajikistan is mountainous, dominated by the towering Pamir peaks, the colossal Fedchenko Glacier, and turquoise alpine lakes.

triviaItems.fact: Shashmaqom classical music, Pamiri rubab lutes, and Navruz mountain spring festivals are cherished traditions of Tajikistan.

cards.name: Tanzania
cards.story: Germany seized mainland Tanganyika in the 1880s and crushed the 1905–07 Maji Maji anti-colonial uprising with a scorched-earth campaign that destroyed crops and villages, killing an estimated 200,000 to 300,000 Africans mostly through engineered famine before Britain took over after World War I. Tanganyika (1961) and Zanzibar (1963)—where the 1964 Zanzibar Revolution killed thousands of Arab and South Asian islanders—merged into Tanzania in April 1964.

environment.biomeLabel: East African Savanna, Rift Crater & Kilimanjaro
environment.summary: Tanzania encompasses endless Serengeti plains, the volcanic Ngorongoro Crater, snow-capped Mount Kilimanjaro, Africa's Great Lakes, and Zanzibar coral islands.

triviaItems.fact: Mount Kilimanjaro, Africa's highest peak, is in Tanzania.
Swahili is a major language in Tanzania.
The spice island of Zanzibar belongs to Tanzania.

cards.name: Thailand
cards.story: Known historically as Siam, Thailand is the only Southeast Asian kingdom never formally colonized by a European empire, though Britain and France coerced Siam through gunboat diplomacy—including the 1893 Paknam crisis—to cede nearly half its tributary territory in Laos, Cambodia, and Malaya by 1909. Inside its borders, state centralization and counterinsurgency in the Muslim-majority Deep South since 2004 have killed over 7,500 people.

environment.biomeLabel: Tropical Monsoon Plains, Limestone Karst & Reefs
environment.summary: Forested northern hills and the fertile Chao Phraya central rice basin extend south into a narrow peninsula of dramatic karst towers and Andaman reefs.

triviaItems.fact: Songkran, the joyous April New Year water festival, is celebrated across Thailand.
The Baht is the currency of Thailand.

cards.name: Togo
cards.story: After centuries of slave trafficking along its coast, Germany colonized Togoland in 1884 using forced labor before Britain and France split it lengthwise after World War I, dividing the Ewe people across an artificial border. Western Togoland voted to join Ghana, while French Togoland became independent Togo in 1960.

environment.summary: Togo forms a slender West African corridor rising from Atlantic coconut beaches and coastal lagoons across the forested Togo Mountains into open northern savanna.

triviaItems.fact: The annual Evala initiation wrestling festival of the Kabyè people in Kara takes place in Togo.

cards.name: Tonga
